column3: NASB supplies “vigorous,” and “on him” is rendered “to himself.”
“From your fear” is rendered “because of your reverence.”
“Held in pledge your brothers” is rendered “taken pledges of your brothers,” and “stripped off the garments of the naked” as “stripped men naked.”
“A person of arm” is rendered “the mighty man,” and “uplifted of face” as “the honorable man.”
“The top of the stars” is rendered “the distant stars.”
“The circle of heaven” is rendered “the vault of heaven.”
“And not an appropriate time” is rendered “before their time.”
The Hebrew has “to them”; NASB keeps it. NASB supplies “And.”
“If not destroyed” is an oath form rendered “Truly … are cut off”; NASB supplies “Saying.”
“You will be built up” is rendered “you will be restored”; NASB supplies “If.”
“Silver of heaps” is rendered “choice silver”; the meaning is uncertain.
The Hebrew is terse; NASB renders “When you are cast down, you will speak with confidence,” and the meaning is uncertain.
“Not an innocent person” is rendered “one who is not innocent”; some read “the innocent,” and the meaning is uncertain.
